entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: My, this is quite the gathering.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Why did they come here, of all places?[n]It's so hot...

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Perhaps they are trying to catch the cool[n]air blowing over the water.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: We are rather interested in entering[n]the water ourselves, if possible...
Where are your swimsuits?
Not dressed like that.
Race you to the water.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: You're talking about special apparel for[n]entering water, yes? Of course we lack[n]such things.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: And we can't go in the water in these[n]outfits... Our master would be none[n]too pleased upon our return.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: We require special apparel for entering[n]the water. Unfortunately, we lack such[n]things.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: We can't go in the water in these outfits...[n]Our master would be none too pleased[n]upon our return.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Someone's grown awfully excited by[n]the sight of the water... Has the heat[n]fried your brain?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Maybe you really should jump into[n]the ocean.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: By the way, I noticed a peculiar group[n]over there...

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I do not know why, but they stand in a[n]loose formation, striking a plastic sphere[n]back and forth...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: It was probably a summoning ritual.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: See? It looks like they're trying to build[n]a shriveled Decarabia army.
Those are starfish.
That's beach volleyball.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: ...They're not Decarabia?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: If they're not summoning, then what[n]are they doing?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Beach volleyball?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Never heard of it. What is it?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I see. So it is a form of human recreation.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Is that some variation of beach volleyball[n]they're playing over there? It looks like[n]they're using a ball as well...

entries.speaker: Blindfolded Man
entries.en: Where's the watermelon?

entries.speaker: Man in a Flashy Outfit
entries.en: Straight, straight! Right, right!

entries.speaker: Woman in a Bikini
entries.en: Too far! Go back! No, not that way!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I know what this is—it's called suika wari,[n]correct?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: From what I've heard, splitting[n]a watermelon with a stick can be[n]a great pleasure...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: How barbaric... What's so fun about that?
It's a form of stress relief.
You picture the melon as somebody.
Watermelon is very tasty.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: So it's part of the destructive tendencies[n]you humans have?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: The game doesn't appear to have any[n]hidden purpose or meaning.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: That is barbaric indeed. So a player dons[n]a blindfold, then imagines the face of[n]someone they dislike?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: If people didn't relieve their stress with[n]games like this, they'd be the ones to[n]crack up eventually—is that it?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Ohhh! So, splitting a watermelon open[n]makes it taste better than simply cutting[n]into it?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Human desire knows no bounds when[n]it comes to food...

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: So this place has more benefits to it[n]than just an ocean breeze...

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Humans can come here to fulfill their[n]desires and release their frustration.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Then, the ocean sweeps up all those[n]feelings and washes them away...

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I must say, I find myself quite impressed[n]with this "Mother Ocean"...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: We now know why humans gather at[n]the beach, so we have determined this[n]request to be complete.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Here is your reward.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: We've been rewarding you every time for[n]these—you'd better take these assignments[n]seriously, Inmate!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: As suggested by the moniker "Mother[n]Ocean," some say humanity was originally[n]born from the ocean.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Perhaps the true reason humans gather[n]here is that their instincts beckon them[n]home.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Hey, Inmate—do you grow nostalgic[n]when you swim in "Mother Ocean"?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Try swimming with a ball and chain on[n]your leg next time. I bet that'll help[n]with your rehabilitation, too.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: It's grown quite hot... You must escort us[n]back now.
I escorted the twins back[n]to the Velvet Room...
